title: Quantized padding + batch-scheduler incompatibility causing intermittent OOMs and accuracy drift
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Summary: After a canary rollout of the new batch-scheduler optimizations, a subset of quantized model serving pods entered OOM/restart loops and several customers reported subtle generation quality regressions. This ticket captures the incident follow-up, immediate mitigations, and long-term engineering work to prevent recurrence. Impact: ~0.6% of production requests for int8 models during the rollout window, with two enterprise customers observing degraded output on RLHF-style prompts.
timeline: 2025-02-24 09:12 UTC - Canary rollout of batch-scheduler v2 began (10% of traffic for quantized models).
2025-02-24 10:03 UTC - Pager alerts: elevated pod restarts on quant-int8 pool (node OOMs).
2025-02-24 10:20 UTC - Ops routed traffic off canary group; rollback initiated for batch-scheduler.
2025-02-24 11:00 UTC - Initial mitigation: reverted scheduler config and scaled up fallback pool.
2025-02-24 14:45 UTC - Metrics: token-level error spike and increase in perplexity on affected prompts identified in canary traces.
2025-02-25 08:30 UTC - Root cause hypothesis formed after trace & core dump analysis.
root_cause: A scheduling change that pads micro-batches to uniform sizes for throughput interacted poorly with the int8 converter's memory layout assumptions. The padding introduced additional KV cache allocations and a rare alignment case that triggered allocator fragmentation on some GPU kernels, causing intermittent OOMs. Separately, the padding caused slightly different tokenization boundaries in the batching edge (rare), exposing a quantization sensitivity in a small RLHF prompt set leading to quality drift. The issue required a combination of scheduling, allocator, and converter safeguards.
immediate_mitigations: Rolled back batch-scheduler v2 to v1 for all quantized-serving pools (rollback completed 2025-02-24 10:20 UTC).
Scaled fallback (fp16) pool for affected customers and pinned critical routes to non-quantized variants for 48 hours.
Hotfix deployed to avoid padding-induced KV cache growth: scheduler returns original batch sizes for quantized models until full fix lands (hotfix PR: GH-Redwood/infra#9876).
Added temporary rate-limit on canary traffic for quantized models to 5% while root-cause analysis completed.
long_term_action_items: Add allocator alignment checks and guardrails in the int8 converter to detect and reject unsupported padding patterns (owner: runtime-team, estimate: 5).
Implement a batching compatibility test suite that runs quantized model traces through upcoming scheduler changes in CI with memory and output-diff thresholds (owner: infra-test, estimate: 8).
Introduce deterministic tokenization boundary tests for batched inputs to catch subtle reorder/padding effects that can expose quantization sensitivity (owner: tokenizer-team, estimate: 3).
Enhance runtime observability: per-batch KV allocation histogram, pad-origin labels, and per-model compatibility score telemetry (owner: observability, estimate: 5).
Create a canary gating policy: scheduler changes must pass quantized-model memory and output-stability gates on canary traffic before rollout (owner: release-eng, estimate: 2).
Post-release customer notification and runbook update: include steps for pinning to non-quantized variants and contact path (owner: support, estimate: 1).
progress_updates: 2025-02-25 - 15:30 UTC - Lucas: Completed heap profiling on one affected node; observed fragmentation spikes correlated with padded KV cache growth.
2025-02-26 - 11:00 UTC - Aisha: Deployed hotfix GH-Redwood/infra#9876 that disables pad-to-max-size for quantized model batches; immediate crash rate dropped to baseline.
2025-02-27 - 09:45 UTC - QA: Began building the batching compatibility tests using recorded production traces (subset of traces stored in GCS: gs://redwood-prod-traces/2025-02-pad-incident).
2025-03-01 - 13:20 UTC - Runtime-team: Drafted allocator alignment guardrail design and shared in #runtime-arch for review.
2025-03-03 - 16:05 UTC - Observability: Prototype telemetry PR opened (GH-Redwood/obs#451) that emits per-batch KV allocation histograms to datadog (staging only).
review_feedback: PM review (Rosa Martinez): Please include a customer communication draft and confirm SLA exposure. Agreed to prepare a one-page incident summary for affected accounts.
Design review (Evan Park): Dashboard heatmaps should surface pad-origin and model-variant side-by-side to make triage faster.
